what_its_for: Clomiphene is used to help women who are having trouble getting pregnant. It works by stimulating your body to release eggs (ovulate). It is also sometimes used in men to help with certain hormone problems related to fertility.
how_to_take: Take clomiphene by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Your doctor will tell you exactly which days of your menstrual cycle to take it — most commonly starting on day 3, 4, or 5 of your period. Follow your doctor's instructions carefully, as timing is very important for this medication to work.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 50 mg (one tablet) taken once a day for 5 days. Your doctor may increase the dose to 100 mg per day for 5 days if 50 mg does not work. Do not take more than your doctor prescribes. Most doctors will not prescribe more than 3 to 6 treatment cycles.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at once. Call your doctor if you miss a dose, because timing is very important with this medication.
storage: Store clomiphene at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medication that is expired — check the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or notice any vision changes, as clomiphene can sometimes affect your vision. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase dizziness and other side effects. Do not take extra doses thinking it will improve your chances of pregnancy — it will not and could be harmful. Avoid becoming pregnant with more than the recommended monitoring, as clomiphene increases the chance of having twins or more.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe pelvic or stomach pain or bloating (this could be a sign of Ovarian Hyperstimulation Syndrome, or OHSS); sudden vision changes, blurring, or seeing flashes of light; shortness of breath or difficulty breathing; rapid weight gain; hot flashes that become very uncomfortable; abnormal vaginal bleeding; signs of a blood clot such as leg pain, swelling, or chest pain. Also contact your doctor if you have not had a period after finishing a treatment cycle, or if you think you may be pregnant.
when_it_works: Ovulation usually happens 5 to 10 days after you finish your 5-day course of clomiphene. Your doctor may use ultrasound or blood tests to check if you ovulated. If you are going to get pregnant with clomiphene, it most often happens within the first 3 treatment cycles. If it has not worked after 3 to 6 cycles, your doctor will discuss other options with you.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do not take clomiphene if you are already pregnant. If you become pregnant during treatment, stop the medication and call your doctor immediately. Breastfeeding: Clomiphene may reduce milk production, so talk to your doctor before using it while breastfeeding. Liver disease: Do not use clomiphene if you have liver problems, as it is processed through the liver. Ovarian cysts: Do not take clomiphene if you currently have ovarian cysts or enlarged ovaries (not related to polycystic ovary syndrome). Older adults: Clomiphene is not typically used in postmenopausal women. Children: This medication is not for use in children.
